analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Materials Oct 27: Gold Outflows, Iron Ore drift, NUE inline (px strength, guide +10%), FCX later, VALE earnings cut, Copper ask., China charts and GAS
key_insights: Iron ore is below $90/t as a weaker BRL compresses the cost curve and nudges the price lower. The desk's message is to hold the line on the iron ore short. FMG is described as a structural short, BHP caught a risk bid rather than an iron ore bid, and RIO sits between the two.

Copper: the DRC-versus-Chile output gap is cited at about 1.35mt. Closing it would require a material SX-EW ramp and depends more on Chile falling than on the DRC growing. A story about the DRC removing the head of its artisanal mining regulator amid a crackdown (300 Chinese nationals detained) is flagged. Copper remains the primary ask in the base case.

After LME week, aluminium is described as bearish, though many think the next $100 move is higher. Zinc is the metal where the market feels most confident underwriting today's price. BOL.SS and TECK.CN both report this week.

NUE reported in line: EPS $5.80, revenue +4% vs consensus, margins modestly below at 20.3%. The Q4 guide implies about +10% upgrades on higher realised pricing. NUE raised its weekly HRC price by $15/st to $1,270/st (CRU at $1,302). The theme is value over volume.

US HRC stays well bid. The very small contango at the front implies a peak into the new year, after which backwardation picks up. The desk likes the back-end roll-up story toward $1,300, which needs no tariff changes to happen.

Germany steel: sentiment at last week's conference was constructive. Market participants look to CBAM and quotas to keep the market tight, targeting a level a bit above the current spot of EUR750, at about EUR800.

MT.NA: Q3 EBITDA estimates have fallen from about $2.15bn to $1.88bn. The stock is at EUR52, and investors are described as looking for a reason to own it. The desk sees little read-through from NUE. The EUR-over-US trade is favoured for 2027.

GS downgrades VALE earnings for 2H26 and 2027 on fuels, freight, production and pricing. 3Q26 EBITDA is forecast at $3.3B (-20% q/q, consensus $3.57B, about 8% below). The forward benchmark iron ore price is $93/t for 2027 vs $100/t for the 2026 average (GSe). Price realisation is forecast down $5/t y/y in 2027 because the product mix is shifting to low-margin products (25% of the portfolio).

Gold: GLD saw its biggest weekly outflow since March. The desk's view is that ETF strength has come from central banks and retail being early, with CTAs short and macro funds not involved. The pain last week was broad.
EGO.US reports later this week. The market is short. The filter press headline is read as a good sign, and the desk says to stick with the name.

FCX is reporting later today. It pre-reported production on 2 October (stock +3.5%): production was better, sales guidance was lowered, and the average selling price was $6.50. Consensus for today: operating EBITDA $3.15bn, EPS $0.81, capex $1.138bn, FCF $967m. GS 2027 estimates are 1,180mlbs Cu and 985k oz Au. The desk is watching for Bagdad FID on the concentrator expansion (target 2H26, capex about $4.5bn, 3-4 years, 200-250m lbs copper).
Norilsk confirms 2026 own-source nickel production guidance. The desk thinks any supply recovery after possible sanctions relief is more a 2028 than a 2027 story.

GLEN: marketing guidance has already been updated (above $5bn, structurally +$300m a year). The desk sees GLEN as a logistics business that benefits from freight cost push, is less worried about Thursday's production print, and is running max size.
TTF gas is up 8% w/w at EUR95/MWh. The Dec26 contract is also EUR95/MWh, implying a 73% market-perceived probability of a low-Mideast-LNG-supply winter (vs 51% last week).

Coffee: a strong 2026/27 crop should push the global market into surplus. Low ICE certified stocks could keep the futures curve in backwardation and front-month prices volatile. The 2027/28 crop is already at risk from Brazil's arabica off-year, uneven flowering after rainfall about 207% above normal, and Vietnam groundwater depleted by El Niño.

CFTC data for the week ending 20 Oct: net managed money notional invested fell $8.1bn to $197bn (grains -$5.7bn, precious metals -$3.6bn, crude +$2.8bn). TTF and Brent have RSI above 70, while palladium, wheat, corn and US natural gas are below 30. Copper selling is noted but not alarming.
